speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are here because your infant has recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing; tell me, at what specific times or during which activities do these breathing difficulties occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion and post-prandial vomiting is highly suggestive of a laryngeal anomaly. Given the child's age and symptoms, do you notice any difficulty with feeding due to choking or coughing, and has he been born prematurely?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The clinical presentation of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, along with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: Laryngeal_Frontal_Side
